Q1: Potassium bromate presents known significant hazards (Tier 1) for carcinogenicity, mutagenicity, reproductive toxicity (CMR), oral exposure (ORL), and organ/systemic effects (OGN). An expanded perspective (Tier 2) on its hazards exists for environmental impacts (ENV), inhalation (IHL), and dermal/eye exposure (SKN), while data for endocrine disruption (EDC) is currently deficient (Tier 4).
Q2: Potassium bromate is identified on several prominent "Lists of Concern," including California's Proposition 65, the IARC Group 2B classification (possibly carcinogenic to humans), and the ChemSEC "Substitute It Now" (SIN) list. Despite its presence on the FDA's "Substances Added to Food" list, this likely pertains to highly regulated conditions involving very low quantities, as its hazardous nature is clearly established.
Q3: Potassium bromate is largely well-characterized, with 5,420 literature references, significantly exceeding the median for the relevant chemical dataset. Its specific molecular formula (BrHO3.K) and a well-defined substance class, alongside only one data-deficient hazard class (EDC4) out of seven, indicate a comprehensive and robust hazard profile.
